items.title: Sensex surges over 1,200 points, Nifty reclaims 23,400 as RIL leads rally
items.description: Indian equity markets experienced a significant surge, primarily driven by Reliance Industries which saw an 11.6% increase. Easing crude oil prices and renewed diplomatic talks regarding Iran contributed positively to investor sentiment. The BSE Sensex rose by more than 1,200 points, while the NSE Nifty exceeded the 23,400 mark. Broader market segments, including metals and cement stocks, also experienced noteworthy gains.

items.title: Sebi allows REITs, InvITs to tap overseas investors through depository receipts
items.description: Sebi has established frameworks allowing real estate investment trusts and infrastructure investment trusts to issue foreign currency denominated depository receipts. This initiative enables them to access capital from overseas markets through international exchanges in GIFT City. To issue depository receipts, unitholder approval will be required, with a majority supporting such moves. Certain restrictions and conditions will apply to participating trusts and existing unitholders.

items.title: We will consider the call for review of LTCG tax: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
items.description: "The circumstances have changed and, therefore, the voices of concern are louder,'' she said at a media event, in reference to reports that her administration has received suggestions to review levies on long-term capital gains (LTCG) for overseas investors. "I quite appreciate that. So, I'll consider all this... Our growth is very important, where people are putting their very best, we are able to see sustained 7(%)-plus growth.''

items.title: D-Street poised for positive start as GIFT Nifty signals gains
items.description: Indian equity markets enjoyed a rally, spurred by robust buying in major stocks such as Reliance Industries. Analysts pegged immediate support for Nifty at 23,200, with resistance encountered at 23,500 and 23,700. Foreign portfolio investors were active buyers, netting Rs 3,115 crore, while domestic institutional investors offloaded shares worth Rs 392 crore. Meanwhile, the rupee dipped by 10 paise to close at 94.

items.title: Stocks in news: ITC, Marico, SBI, Yatra Online, NSE, Container Corp and Sun Pharma
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks experienced gains, with Nifty nearing the 23,500 resistance level and strong corporate earnings reported. ITC faced a decline in consolidated net profit, impacted by the cigarette business, despite revenue growth. Marico saw a significant rise in net profit and expanding EBITDA margins during the quarter. Container Corporation of India reported a subdued performance with a slight decline in net profit compared to last year.

items.title: RIL shares surge 11.6% on strong Q2 earnings; analysts see further upside
items.description: Reliance Industries has seen an impressive 11.6% surge in stock price, following quarterly earnings that exceeded expectations. This remarkable rise represents the company's most significant increase in over six years. Analysts are optimistic about future growth, crediting this success to strong performance in the O2C sector and increased institutional buying. Brokerage firms predict potential earnings upgrades will further boost stock valuation.

items.title: FPI holding hits multi-year lows in 70% of top 100 Indian companies
items.description: Foreign investors have significantly reduced their holdings in nearly 70% of India's leading companies in recent years. Major firms, including banks and IT sectors, are seeing foreign ownership decline to multi-decade lows. This decrease in foreign investments mirrors diminished expectations for growth in India relative to other global markets. Although some companies experience slight increases in foreign ownership, they still remain at historical lows.

items.title: Stock Radar: Coforge stock hits fresh record high in October; will the rally continue in November 2026?
items.description: Coforge Ltd has achieved a fresh record high and has shown strong growth in recent weeks. The stock’s upward momentum suggests potential targets above 2,200 levels in the next few weeks. Analysts recommend a buy-on-dips strategy, maintaining a strict stop loss at 1,810. Technical indicators indicate sustained strength and positive momentum in the stock's performance. Investors are encouraged to consider these positions as the market evolves.

items.title: Aditya Birla Lifestyle bets on festive demand
items.description: The company, which owns brands such as Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly and Peter England, reported flat like-for-like sales growth in September, against 5.3% for the second quarter of FY27. The slowdown comes just as the full impact of price increases begins to flow through in the December quarter, making consumer acceptance and discounting critical to sustaining growth.

items.title: Institutional investors step up bets on private credit as insurers, pension funds and DFIs back new funds
items.description: Institutional investors are now allocating more funds to private credit, significantly from insurance companies and pension funds. Neo Alternative Asset Managers has seen its second fund receive 22-25% contributions from these investors. Ascertis Credit's fourth fund also attracted commitments exceeding $700 million from multiple institutional investors. With increased interest in private credit, annual investment opportunities are now estimated around ₹1 lakh crore.

items.title: A month after RBI’s rate hike, banks start raising deposit rates as liquidity shrinks, Bank of India the latest to move
items.description: Domestic banks are beginning to increase their deposit rates due to shrinking liquidity conditions in the market. Bank of India recently announced a rate hike on deposits for various maturities, including a special 500-day option. This decision reflects the growing cost of deposits in the banking system as demand for credit rises. Banking system liquidity has significantly decreased from its peak in early September.
